$comment: The gate. Every tag marked `covered: true` must be claimed by at least one test whose
NAME contains the tag. `scripts/check-invariants.mjs` fails the build when a covered
tag has zero tests, when a pending tag already has one, and when a retirement has no
This exists because a coverage floor cannot see these. Every invariant is a NEGATIVE —
'never posts twice', 'never fires after teardown', 'never auto-dismisses'. Deleting the
F-37-1c test does not move line coverage by a single point.
`covered: false` means the tag is known and not yet claimed. S1 builds the scaffold and
claims none of them: each later unit writes the test and flips its own tags to true.
The `unit` field names the unit that owns the tag, from the breakdown in
`retired: true` means the tag describes a branch this backend cannot reach, so no test
can ever claim it. It needs a `why`, and acquiring a test is an error rather than
progress — the reason was wrong. Retired tags are counted separately and excluded from
the exit criterion, because leaving them pending makes that criterion unreachable and
hides permanent zeroes among the real gaps.
The first 29 tags are 1.0's list, carried over. The seven below them are 2.0 work: the
async diagnosis panel (spec section 4.1), the review screen (section 3.2), the design
tokens (section 4.2), and the serve idempotence of trap T13 (section 5).
